reviews.scope: Identifying real and imaginary parts of each operand
reviews.reason: Componentwise addition and subtraction combine real parts with real parts and imaginary parts with imaginary parts. A student who cannot pick out a and b in a+bi cannot carry this out.

The first criterion asks students to compute the sample mean. That is arithmetic mean computation and interpretation as central tendency, applied to sample data. No representation of the task avoids computing a mean.

reviews.scope: Comparing sample means and treating them as population estimates
reviews.reason: Case studies compare two sample means and call the conclusion an estimate. That draws directly on using a sample mean to estimate a population center. The median part of the prerequisite is not needed.

reviews.scope: Event as a subset of the sample space
reviews.reason: P(A)=m/n counts the sample points that belong to event A. That only makes sense once an event is understood as a subset of the finite sample space. Event operations are not needed.

reviews.scope: Each axis as a number line with origin, direction, unit
reviews.reason: The space coordinate system is defined as three mutually perpendicular number lines. Reading x, y and z presupposes origin, positive direction and unit length on each axis.

reviews.scope: Recognizing and computing the denominator as normal vector magnitude
reviews.reason: The criterion explicitly says the denominator is the magnitude of the normal vector. That needs the coordinate formula for the magnitude of a space vector, not a two-point distance procedure.

reviews.scope: Converting point-slope form to general form
reviews.reason: One criterion is converting point-slope form to Ax+By+C=0. Students must read and manipulate y-y0=k(x-x0), so knowing point-slope form is necessary for that criterion.

reviews.scope: Reading point coordinates to form coordinate differences
reviews.reason: The distance formula takes differences of horizontal and vertical coordinates. Students must understand what plane coordinates mean before those differences can be seen as legs of a right triangle.

reviews.scope: Meaning of center-to-line distance as shortest perpendicular length
reviews.reason: Comparing d with r decides intersection only because d is the perpendicular, shortest distance from the center to any point of the line. That rests on the perpendicular-segment concept.

reviews.scope: Finding the quantity after several periods at fixed ratio
reviews.reason: Treating the growth factor as a common ratio and finding the value after n periods is the general term a1q^(n-1). Repeated multiplication just computes that same term step by step.

reviews.scope: Row n as binomial coefficients of (a+b)^n
reviews.reason: The node defines row n as the binomial coefficients of (a+b)^n. Reading an entry by that convention requires knowing that the binomial expansion has coefficients C(n,k).

reviews.scope: Explaining adjacent-entry sums and symmetry with combination numbers
reviews.reason: The criterion asks students to explain adjacent sums using combination numbers. That explanation is exactly C(n,k)+C(n,k-1)=C(n+1,k). The triangle's symmetry likewise reflects C(n,k)=C(n,n-k).

reviews.scope: Building distribution tables for multistage experiments
reviews.reason: The stated criteria only complete a missing probability from the total of 1 and check that a table is legal. Multistage multiplication is common when building tables but lies outside this scope.
reviews.counterexample: Given a table with one unknown entry, students find it by subtracting the others from 1 without any multiplication rule.

reviews.scope: Interpreting expectation as a probability-weighted average
reviews.reason: The criterion requires explaining expectation as a weighted average, with probabilities playing the role of weights. That interpretation presupposes the weighted mean concept, not just the ordinary arithmetic mean.

reviews.scope: Evaluating C(n,k) in the binomial probability
reviews.reason: The factorial formula is the standard way to get C(n,k). The coefficient can also be read from Yang Hui's triangle or found by counting success paths, so the formula belongs to one method.
reviews.counterexample: For n=4, k=2 a student reads 6 from row 4 of Yang Hui's triangle or lists the success arrangements.
